section.t: The full-collection path establishes its capture, exact-source, exact-creation-view and exact-receiver-view premises only when every required operational observation matches and all five deployment predicates are approved. Its composition premise additionally requires no unresolved finalization binding; its receiver-binding premise requires no unresolved inbox binding. Derived premises retain the capture basis and transitive accepted assumptions. These observations do not prove administrator honesty, credential exclusivity, absence of hidden publication or storage correctness. A missing assumption or unestablished observation leaves this path's population claims not-established.
The support declaration and additional limits of the reference implementation are described separately in .

The aggregate receipt_binding check reports not-evaluated if not attempted, unresolved if any retained candidate has unresolved B interpretation, refuted if all candidate interpretations are resolved and at least one is invalid, and supported if every candidate has a valid B binding, including the vacuous empty case. An invalid candidate remains visible even when another candidate makes the aggregate unresolved. Identity conflicts are separately retained; this aggregate does not decide creation or delivery outcomes. This profile uses only the four active check states specified in and does not emit the reserved conflicted state. Logical derivation conflicts are handled separately by Coverage aggregation.

section.name: Timestamp Encoding
section.t: Both collected_at and actual-result evaluation_time MUST use the following restricted UTC form of , expressed in ABNF . The grammar matches the entire decoded string without leading or trailing whitespace. DIGIT is imported from , Appendix B.1.

The four-digit year is 0001 through 9999. The month and day MUST form a valid Gregorian calendar date, including the leap-year rule. Hours are 00 through 23; minutes and seconds are 00 through 59. The optional fraction has one through six digits. Only uppercase T and Z are allowed. Leap-second notation, offsets other than Z, reduced-precision or week dates, comma fractions and extra suffixes are rejected as INPUT_INVALID. This deliberately narrower language is part of profile 0.2.0; it is not silently imposed on an artifact from another profile revision.

Examples are 2026-10-21T09:00:00Z and 2026-10-21T09:00:00.123456Z. Timestamp syntax establishes neither clock accuracy nor an authenticated observation time. Timestamps do not replace logical seal coordinates or prove commit order.

section.name: Input, Reports and Semantic Validation
section.t: The five schemas listed here are normative structural contracts using JSON Schema 2020-12 . They do not replace the semantic requirements of this appendix. JSON follows , with valid UTF-8, unique member names, no unpaired surrogates and no nonfinite numbers. Insignificant whitespace and object member order do not change logical meaning; every artifact digest nevertheless binds exact supplied bytes. There is no canonical-JSON transformation before hashing.

section.t: The manifest supplies profile and version, a request naming coverage/0.2.0 and unique requested claim IDs, detached snapshot and policy references, a detached assumption-policy reference, and evidence references. Every artifact reference has exactly name, sha256 and octets. A name is a flat relative artifact name, never a path or network URL; all named artifacts have unique names distinct from the manifest name. Every length and SHA-256 digest MUST be verified. The adapter MUST NOT fetch URLs or execute artifact contents. Evidence IDs are unique and MUST NOT use the reserved IDs input-snapshot or pinned-policy. An evidence kind names material to inspect, not a trusted boolean.

The adapter report has exactly the nine checks in the mapping table above. Each check records not-evaluated, supported, refuted or unresolved, with evidence references and a reason. References resolve to manifest evidence IDs or the two reserved artifact IDs. Supported and refuted checks require inspected evidence. Not-evaluated means unattempted; unresolved means attempted without sufficient basis. adapter_status=evaluated means all checks were attempted, not that all passed. The report's input_sha256 hashes the exact manifest bytes and MUST be present for an evaluated report; null means those bytes were unavailable or no input was supplied. An adapter report does not override a logical prerequisite.

The structural schema retains conflicted as a reserved adapter check state. A producer of this profile version MUST NOT emit it, and a semantic validator MUST reject an adapter report containing it as an invalid profile report. Structural acceptance of that reserved value does not make the report semantically valid. This restriction does not change the logical Coverage aggregation of conflicting derivations.

The logical result has contract CoverageResult/0.2.0, rule set coverage/0.2.0 and the profile identifiers above. It supports all ten claim IDs: supplied-correspondence, source-complete, source-sound, source-exact, creation-complete, creation-sound, creation-exact, delivery-complete, delivery-exact and empty-actions. An evaluated claim has outcome supported, refuted or not-established; an unevaluated claim has a reason, no outcome and no derivations.

Actual results use artifact_kind=evaluation-result, identify the evaluator and version, and bind the real input manifest, pinned policies, evaluation timestamp and all three seal coordinates. The timestamp MUST be validated as a date and time, not merely accepted because of a schema format annotation. Null cutoffs are permitted only for constructed-example, which consumers MUST reject as evaluation evidence. A missing actual seal yields a collection error rather than an invented bound result. Declaring a coordinate does not authenticate it. specifies the required timestamp language.

The serialized context's fixed scope value is durable-commits-to-coverage_pg.action_ledger-in-epoch, its receipt_stream is coverage_pg.finalization_ledger, and its payload_projection is sha256-of-exact-action-payload-bytes. These exact wire identifiers designate the ledger semantics defined here and do not require a private SQL or programming-language interface.

The serialized context object and its enclosing profile, profile_version, evaluator and assumption_policy fields jointly encode the logical context required by . The mapping below makes explicit the fields and fixed profile semantics used by the result schema in . These constants do not admit arbitrary tenant partitions, resource kinds or business-action meanings under the same scope identifier; changing those meanings requires another identified binding or profile revision.

Structural validity alone makes neither an imported result nor its premises trusted.

Both usable support and usable refutation produce not-established with a derivation-conflict diagnostic retaining both branches. Downstream claim dependencies require the aggregated claim to be supported; selecting a favorable derivation from a conflicted claim is forbidden. Family implications operate on derivations before aggregation without creating cyclic outcome dependencies.

References use evidence:<manifest-id>, input-snapshot#<JSON-Pointer>, premise:<id>, claim:<claim-id>, derivation:<id> or transformation:<id> as applicable. JSON Pointer follows . Detached-artifact references are bound by their manifest digest. Premise and assumption references use premise IDs, claim dependencies use claim IDs, and diagnostic references use diagnostic IDs. Resolution alone does not confer trust. Assumptions, premises, diagnostics, transformations and derivations are ordered lexicographically by stable IDs. Claims preserve requested order followed by dependency claims in claim-ID order. Retained invalid-member references and normalization transformations MUST preserve access to the raw evidence.

section.t: The following cases specify observable expectations, not a claim that any deployment has passed them. Except where a row varies a prerequisite, assume authenticated complete sealed populations, the exact approved context and policies, all five accepted deployment predicates, no identity conflicts and available cryptography. Initially two distinct actions each have one correctly bound final receipt, and both receipts are in the recipient inbox. For the illustrative consumer decisions, the consumer requires creation-exact and delivery-exact. Every negative expectation requires its indicated positive membership witness and complete search basis; fixture labels or a hidden test oracle cannot establish those premises.

section.t: Additional encoding cases exercise the original received bytes: duplicate JSON members; extra closed-object fields; alternate, duplicate or unordered CBOR keys; forbidden algorithm -8; wrong protected key ID; detached payload; extra COSE header or tag; trailing bytes; and all stated size and depth boundaries. A malformed retained finalization exercises an invalid B edge while remaining in its population; the same defect in the collection authentication record prevents that record from establishing capture. Exact action UUIDs, payload hashes, policy digests, recipient, issuer and outer-to-inner receipt identities MUST each be checked rather than inferred from a valid signature.

Admission cases include rollback, lost commit response followed by durable recollection, writers blocked behind each seal, whole-transaction retry on serialization failure, rejected post-seal admission and inability of an ordinary sender to admit inbox records. Constructed assertions can test parser and inference behavior but do not observe these database events. Deployment conformance requires the applicable checks against its actual authenticated endpoints, storage, principal bindings and publication and acknowledgment discipline. This appendix does not claim power-loss, storage-fault, failover, restore or independently operated interoperability evidence merely from successful process-crash or same-host tests.

section.name: Reference Implementation (Informative)
section.t: This appendix records implementation experience from the earlier prototype identified in . It is not an implementation or conformance claim for the profile specified in . The prototype's single-collection choice predates the current normative selection rule; the current profile also fixes timestamp, assumption-interval, approval and failure behavior that requires separate implementation validation. The earlier code and frozen trial artifacts retain their original identities. This informative account adds no requirements.

section.name: Supported Evidence Path and Implementation Limits
section.t: The bounded reference path accepts exactly one manifest evidence item of kind collection-provenance; it rejects extra or absent branches with EVIDENCE_MISSING rather than ignoring possible conflicts. The earlier prototype also reports EVIDENCE_MISSING for a sole different recognized evidence kind; the current profile instead specifies NOT_IMPLEMENTED for that case in . This historical behavior is not the normative selection contract. It does not implement alternate evidence families, the P5 receipt-view substitution path, the N5 source-counterexample path or a WEXP Core mapping. Its support paths are P1, P2a, P2b, P3, P4a, P4b, P4c, P6 and P8; its refutation paths are N1, N2a, N2b, N3, N4a, N4b and N6, with P7 and N7 family transport. It returns all ten claims, marking unrequested claims as dependencies. Validation of its generated dependency graph does not make it an importer of arbitrary CoverageResult objects. It reads only flat local regular nonsymlink files and additionally bounds its manifest to 1 MiB. These are declared limits of that path, not a reduction of the earlier profile's input schema's zero-to-128 evidence entries or seven permitted evidence kinds.

section.name: Recomputing Consumer Interface
section.t: The reference consumer recomputes evaluation from the evidence package and external pins; it does not accept a supplied result object as authority. Its caller supplies a nonempty list of unique required claim IDs and an expected context object with exactly these six fields: database_incarnation, epoch_id, recipient_id, action_cutoff, creation_cutoff, receiver_cutoff. Their values must equal the evaluated context exactly. This consumer interface is one bounded application of the profile, not a requirement that every Coverage consumer recompute results.

Invalid required claims or an expected context with a missing or extra field is an INPUT_INVALID interface error. For a valid request, the consumer returns hold for unavailable evaluation, unestablished authentication or any context-value mismatch before considering claim outcomes. With matching context, any refuted required claim produces reject; all required claims supported produces accept; otherwise it returns hold. Its result fields are decision, reason, required_claims, input_sha256, inherited_assumptions, meaning, and evaluation. They carry the decision and explanation, requested claim list, inspected manifest digest when available, sorted unique inherited assumption IDs, an explanation of the decision's Coverage-only meaning, and an object with adapter and coverage fields. The latter is null when no CoverageResult was obtained. Explanation text is not a stable interoperability identifier. Acceptance is conditional on that context and those assumptions; it is not a Core accept verdict or production certification.

section.name: Native Reconciliation Comparison
section.t: A plain set-and-binding reconciliation baseline may share input authentication, candidate normalization and receipt verification with the evaluator. Agreement then tests the rule and result layer, not independent capture or cryptographic verification, and does not establish superiority of one representation.
